title: 20 Must-Read Books on Building with Large Language Models(LLMs)

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Today we're doing something a little different. We're not talking about code repositories, but about the books that can help you become a sharper LLM engineer. Whether you're building AI apps, fine-tuning models, or just curious about how this tech works under the hood, this curated list is designed for developers like you. Stick around. You might just find your next must readad.

sections.title: AI Engineering
paragraphs: First up, we've got AI engineering, building applications with foundation models. This isn't just another AI book. It's a roadmap for developers who actually want to build and ship real applications with LLMs and other foundation models. Chip breaks down how AI engineering is different from traditional ML engineering, introduces the modern AI stack, and tackles one of the toughest challenges in the field, evaluation. From prompt engineering to retrieval, augmented generation, fine-tuning, agents, and data set engineering, this book dives deep into the techniques you'll actually use day-to-day as an engineer.

sections.title: Build a Large Language Model
paragraphs: Next on the list is Build a Large Language Model from Scratch by Sebastian Rashka. This one is an absolute gem for engineers who don't just want to use LLMs, but actually understand them from the inside out. Rashka walks you through designing, coding, and training your very own GPT style model, starting with attention mechanisms all the way to fine-tuning for tasks like classification and instruction following. What's really cool, you can do it all on a regular laptop. No massive server bills required with over 360 pages of clear explanations, diagrams, and hands-on examples. This book makes the blackbox of LLM transparent. And yes, it even comes with GitHub code to back it all up.

sections.title: Building LLM Powered Applications
paragraphs: Our third pick is building LLM powered applications by Valentina Alto. What makes it stand out is the practical use of Langchain, a lightweight Python framework to orchestrate prompts, memory, and tools inside your applications. Across 340 plus pages, you'll explore everything from embedding LLMs into real world software to building chat bots, recommendation engines, and even multimodal apps that go beyond text into vision and audio. It also covers vector databases, fine-tuning, and the ethical side of deploying these systems. [Music]

sections.title: Building LLMs for Production
paragraphs: Next up, we've got building LLMs for production. This 460 plus page guide is designed for developers who want to move beyond prototypes and build productionready AI systems. It covers the full life cycle from fundamentals of LLM theory to practical methods like prompting, fine-tuning, and retrieval augmented generation, also known as RAG. That means it's packed with diverse insights, real world projects, and even collab notebooks you can run immediately. The book walks you through frameworks like Langchain and Llama Index, teaches you how to build advanced retrieval pipelines, deploy and optimize models, and most importantly, make them more reliable and scalable.
[Music]

sections.title: Creating Production-Ready LLMs
paragraphs: Up next is creating production ready LLMs. This 500 plus page powerhouse is your complete guide to taking large language models from concept to real world deployment. It goes beyond coding prototypes, showing you how to train, optimize, fine-tune, and deploy LLMs in production environments across industries like healthcare, finance, and education. You'll explore core architectures like GPT, BERT, and T5. Tackle distributed training on GPUs and TPUs, and master prompt engineering to squeeze the best performance out of your models. The book also dives into challenges often overlooked, debugging, edge cases, scaling, and even ethical compliance so your models are robust, reliable, and responsible.

sections.title: Developing Apps with GPT-4 and ChatGPT
paragraphs: Next on our list is developing apps with GPT4 and chat GPT. This is a concise 155page guide aimed at Python developers who want to quickly get hands-on with GPT4 and chat GPT. It covers everything from text generation and question answering to content summarization and it walks you step by step through the Python APIs that power these models. Beyond the basics, the book also touches on advanced techniques like prompt engineering, fine-tuning, langchain, and even plugins, giving you a fast track to building more sophisticated AI applications with clear examples and a GitHub repository of Python code. This is a practical resource for developers looking to integrate LLMs directly into their projects.

sections.title: Generative AI on AWS
paragraphs: Next up, we have Generative AI on AWS. This 309 page guide is perfect for developers, ML practitioners, and business leaders who want to apply generative AI in real world settings. It covers the full life cycle of generative AI projects from defining use cases and selecting models to fine-tuning retrieval augmented generation and even reinforcement learning from human feedback. What makes this book unique is its focus on multimodal reasoning. The book also shows how to leverage AWS services like Amazon Bedrock to deploy models efficiently and introduces libraries such as Langchain and React to orchestrate agents and actions.

sections.title: Generative AI with LangChain
paragraphs: Next up, we have Generative AI. This 360 page guide is perfect for developers who want to harness the power of Langchain to build LLM applications like chat bots, questionans answering systems, and AI assistance. The book dives into the fundamentals of transformer models, attention mechanisms, and prompt engineering, all while providing practical examples for production ready applications. What sets this book apart is its focus on real world deployment. You'll learn to automate tasks, perform data analysis, fine-tune models, and even interact privately with documents using open- source LLMs, all through Lang Chain.

sections.title: Hands-On Large Language Models
paragraphs: Next up is Hands-On Large Language Models: Language Understanding and Generation. This 425page book is highly visual and educational, making complex LLM concepts easy to grasp. It's ideal for developers and engineers who want to understand how transformer-based language models work and how to apply them in real world tasks like text generation, summarization, semantic search, and clustering. The book covers everything from token embeddings and transformer architectures to advanced techniques like retrieval augmented generation in context learning and fine-tuning models for specific applications. [Music]

sections.title: LangChain Crash Course
paragraphs: Next, we have Langchain Crash Course. This is a short, punchy, 88page guide designed to get you building LLM powered apps fast. If you've ever wanted to spin up a chatbot, document Q&A system, or even a Medium article generator with OpenAI models, this is the book to start with. Greg Lim takes a hands-on step-by-step approach, walking you through Langchain fundamentals, prompt templates, chains, agents, memory management, and even integrating custom documents like PDFs and YouTube content. Every section is bite-sized so you can code along without feeling overwhelmed.

sections.title: Large Language Models
paragraphs: Up next is large language models, a deep dive bridging theory and practice. This 506-page book is a comprehensive deep dive into LLMs, perfect for developers, researchers, and data scientists who want to understand both the theory and real world applications of these models. It covers everything from transformer architectures and pre-training to fine-tuning, reinforcement learning for alignment, and multimodal LLMs that process text, audio, images, and even robotics inputs. The book is packed with practical tutorials, over 200 data sets, 50 plus strategies to address ethical challenges, and more than 200 benchmarks for evaluating LLM performance.

sections.title: LLM Engineer's Handbook
paragraphs: Next, we have LLM engineers handbook. This book is a practical hands-on guide for AI engineers and NLP professionals who want to take LLMs from concept to production. It emphasizes LLM ops best practices, teaching you how to build scalable, modular, and cost-effective end-to-end LLM systems. You'll learn to manage data pipelines, implement supervised fine-tuning, optimize inference, and deploy models using cloud tools like AWS. The book also covers advanced techniques like preference alignment, continuous training, and rag pipelines, making it ideal for real world LLM applications.

sections.title: LLMs in Production
paragraphs: Next, we have LLMs in production. It covers the full life cycle from understanding LLM fundamentals, evaluating when to use pre-built models versus building your own to fine-tuning, scaling, and deploying models to the cloud or even edge devices like Raspberry Pi. The book also walks you through advanced techniques such as LoRa, RLHF, prompt engineering, and operational best practices for chat bots, coding assistants, and other AI applications. What makes it stand out is its hands-on approach with real projects, including a cloud-based chatbot, a VS Code code completion extension, and edge deployment examples.

sections.title: Prompt Engineering for Generative AI
paragraphs: Next, we have prompt engineering for generative AI. If you've ever struggled to make AI models behave the way you want, this book teaches you the principles of prompt engineering to transform your requests into consistent, highquality results. You'll learn the five pillars of prompting, how to structure AI interactions, and advanced techniques for both text and image generation. The book also dives into lang chain integration, vector databases, and building autonomous agents with memory and tools, giving you practical guidance for productionready AI applications.

sections.title: Prompt Engineering for LLMs
paragraphs: Next up is prompt engineering for LLMs, the art and science of building large language model based applications. It's ideal for developers and AI enthusiasts who want to communicate effectively with LLMs, turning ideas into precise model friendly prompts. You'll learn how to design prompt strategies, assemble context elements efficiently, and apply advanced techniques like fshot learning, chain of thought prompting, and rag. The book balances philosophical foundations with practical workflows, giving you confidence to build robust LLM powered applications. Next, we have quick start guide to large language models, second edition. It covers everything from chat GPT, Alama

sections.title: Quick Start Guide to Large Language Models
paragraphs: 3, Claude 3, and other open and closed source models to embeddings, fine-tuning, rag chat bots, and even multimodal AI systems. You'll learn key concepts like tokenization, attention, pre-training, and transfer learning along with advanced techniques for prompt engineering, semantic search, and custom embeddings. The book also guides you through deployment, scaling, performance optimization, and RHF RLF alignment for conversational agents.

sections.title: RAG-Driven Generative AI
paragraphs: Next up is ragdriven generative AI. Using frameworks like Llama Index, Deep Lake, and vector databases like Pine Cone, you'll learn to link every AI response to its source document for traceable, reliable outputs. The book covers everything from scaling rag pipelines, combining text and image data, optimizing for performance, and integrating human feedback to creating multimodal conversational agents. If you're an AI engineer, data scientist, or MLOps professional, this guide gives you the tools to build robust productionready AI systems grounded in real world data.

sections.title: Super Study Guide
paragraphs: If you're looking for a concise, illustrated guide to the inner workings of large language models, check out Super Study Guide, Transformers and Large Language Models. This 247page book breaks down LLMs in a clear, approachable way, perfect for interviews, projects, or satisfying your AI curiosity. It starts with the foundations of neural networks, moves through embeddings and transformers, and explains key architectures like BERT, GPT, and T5. You'll also get hands-on guidance on prompt engineering, parameter efficient fine-tuning, and preference tuning, plus practical applications like sentiment analysis, machine translation, and retrieval augmented generation.

sections.title: Building Secure AI Applications
paragraphs: As LLMs become central to AI applications, security has never been more critical. That's why you need the developers playbook for large language model security. Drawing from the collective expertise behind the OASP top 10 for LLMs, it equips developers and security teams to safeguard AI applications from threats like prompt injection, overexposure, and misuse. Learn how to identify vulnerabilities, protect critical trust boundaries, and deploy defenses that keep your AI systems reliable and safe. Whether you're building a new AI application or adding features to an existing product, this book is your road map to responsible, secure LLM deployment.

sections.title: What Is ChatGPT Doing
paragraphs: Curious about what's really going on inside chat GPT? Steven Wolfrram, a pioneer in computational science, takes you on a deep yet readable dive into the mechanics behind this AI marvel in Yinth. And what is chat GPT doing and why does it work? In just over 100 pages, Wolram unpacks how Chat GPT combines neural networks, embeddings, and probabilitydriven language generation to produce humanlike text. From training intricacies to the hidden structure of meaning, this book connects cutting edge AI with fundamental questions about language and thought. If you want to truly understand why Chat GPT works and what makes it so powerful, this is your essential guide.
